Businesses With Fully AI-Ready Data Report Broad or Strong AI ROI at More Than Six Times (6.5x) the Rate of Businesses Whose Data is Partially Ready

, /PRNewswire/ -- Sixty-five percent of businesses plan to increase spending on AI over the next twelve months, yet only 28% report broad or strong returns from AI efforts, unchanged from last quarter, according to Dun & Bradstreet's latest AI Momentum survey of 10,000 businesses across 32 countries. Only 8% of businesses report that their enterprise data is fully ready to support AI at scale, while 33% describe it as mostly ready and 44% as partially ready. Companies are investing in AI faster than they are readying their data foundation to support it.

The survey finds 81% of businesses with enterprise data that is fully ready for AI are obtaining broad or strong ROI, compared with 12% of those whose data is only partially ready. The pattern is also apparent at the regional level. Eastern Europe (31%), Asia Pacific (30%) and Western Europe (30%) report the highest rates of broad or strong ROI, as well as the highest shares of mostly or fully AI-ready data (41-43%). The Americas and Africa trail on both measures.

The Americas show the starkest mismatch between AI investment and data readiness, and businesses there have the most to gain by getting their data ready. Businesses in the Americas are among the most likely to increase AI spending (approximately 68%), yet the region reports the second-lowest rates of broad or strong ROI (23%) and mostly or fully AI-ready data (37%).

"What stands out this quarter is how much data readiness matters. The organizations whose data is ready for AI are seeing broad returns at a much higher rate than everyone else, even as returns overall have leveled off," said Gary Kotovets, Chief Data & Analytics Officer at Dun & Bradstreet. "The models themselves are very capable. What makes the difference between a pilot and real P&L impact is whether the AI is working from verified business context. That's what we do at Dun & Bradstreet. The D&B Commercial Graph™ has already worked out who a business is and how it's connected, so the AI can start from verified information instead of burning tokens trying to figure that out on its own."

Data readiness has not kept pace with AI investment this year, creating a persistent barrier to scaling returns. From Q3 to Q4, the share of businesses reporting fully AI-ready data rose from 6% to 8%, while the share reporting broad or strong ROI held steady at 28%. However, that gain is concentrated at the top, as the share of organizations describing their data as "mostly ready" fell from 36% to 33%. Partial readiness is where most businesses get stuck, with 57% of those with partially ready data reporting only pockets of ROI, compared with 16% of those fully ready. Organizations with higher data readiness are more likely to report broad, repeatable returns, while those with less-ready data lag behind.

Key Q4 survey findings include:

AI continues to move into production

  • Nearly all businesses (98%) report active AI initiatives.
  • Spending intent is broad-based: 60–68% of businesses in every region expect to increase AI spending, led by the Americas and Western Europe, both at approximately 68%.
  • 37% are scaling AI pilots into production, up from 34% in Q3.

Data readiness is strongly associated with AI ROI

  • Businesses with fully AI-ready data report broad or strong AI ROI at more than six times (6.5x) the rate of businesses whose data is partially ready.
  • 81% of businesses with enterprise data that is fully ready for AI are obtaining broad or strong ROI, compared with 12% of businesses whose data is only partially ready.
  • On strong ROI alone, the gap is wider still: 55% of businesses with fully ready data report strong ROI, compared with 2% of those with low or no data readiness.
  • Regionally, Eastern Europe, Asia Pacific and Western Europe lead on both broad or strong ROI (30–31%) and mostly or fully AI-ready data (41–43%), while the Americas (23% and 37%) and Africa (21% and 33%) trail.

AI returns remain stable

  • 28% report broad or strong AI ROI, unchanged from Q3.
  • 44% report "pockets of ROI" on some AI pilots, while just 9% say most pilots have scaled with clear gains.

Enterprise data is not yet fully ready for AI at scale

  • 8% of businesses report their enterprise data is "fully ready" to support AI at scale.
  • 44% describe their data as "partially ready" and 33% as "mostly ready."

"The next phase of AI adoption will be defined less by access to models and more by the quality of the information those models can use," said Kotovets. "Enterprises that invest in verified identity, connected data and decision-ready context will be better positioned to scale AI with greater speed, confidence and control."

The Dun & Bradstreet AI Momentum Survey is a quarterly global survey of 10,000 businesses across 32 countries that tracks enterprise AI adoption, investment, deployment and business outcomes over time.

About Dun & Bradstreet

Dun & Bradstreet provides the verified commercial identity foundation for enterprises to deploy AI at scale. The company originated the D‑U‑N‑S® Number in 1963, now the global standard for identifying commercial entities. Anchored by this identifier, the D&B Commercial Graph™ structures and connects business identity consistently across systems, enabling AI to operate on accurate, validated data. Since 1841, businesses of every size have relied on Dun & Bradstreet to navigate change and accelerate growth. For more information, visit www.dnb.com.

SOURCE Dun & Bradstreet, Inc.

translation.html:
数据已完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业，报告获得广泛或强劲 AI 投资回报的比例，是数据仅部分就绪企业的六倍以上（6.5 倍）

，/美通社/ -- 根据邓白氏最新的 AI Momentum 调查，65% 的企业计划在未来十二个月增加 AI 支出，但仅有 28% 的企业报告其 AI 项目获得了广泛或强劲的回报，与上一季度持平。该调查覆盖 32 个国家的 10,000 家企业。仅有 8% 的企业表示，其企业数据已完全准备好支持大规模 AI 应用，33% 表示基本就绪，44% 表示部分就绪。企业对 AI 的投资速度，正超过其为支持 AI 而完善数据基础的速度。

调查发现，在企业数据已完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业中，81% 正获得广泛或强劲的投资回报；而在数据仅部分就绪的企业中，这一比例为 12%。这一趋势在地区层面也很明显。东欧（31%）、亚太地区（30%）和西欧（30%）报告获得广泛或强劲投资回报的比例最高，其数据基本或完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业占比也最高（41–43%）。美洲和非洲在这两项指标上均落后。

美洲的 AI 投资与数据就绪程度之间的失衡最为明显，该地区企业通过让数据做好准备，有望获得的收益也最大。 美洲企业增加 AI 支出的意愿位居前列（约 68%），但该地区报告获得广泛或强劲投资回报的比例（23%），以及数据基本或完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业占比（37%），均为各地区第二低。

邓白氏首席数据与分析官 Gary Kotovets 表示：“本季度最突出的一点，是数据就绪程度的影响有多大。尽管整体回报已趋于平稳，数据已具备 AI 应用条件的组织获得广泛回报的比例，仍远高于其他组织。模型本身的能力已经很强。从试点走向实际损益影响，关键在于 AI 是否基于经过验证的业务背景信息开展工作。这正是邓白氏所做的事情。D&B Commercial Graph™ 已经厘清了一家企业的身份及其关联关系，因此 AI 可以从经过验证的信息出发，无需消耗 token 自行摸索这些信息。”

今年，数据就绪程度未能跟上 AI 投资的步伐，持续阻碍企业扩大回报规模。从第三季度到第四季度，报告数据已完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业占比从 6% 升至 8%，而报告获得广泛或强劲投资回报的企业占比保持在 28%。然而，这一进展集中在就绪程度最高的企业，称其数据“基本就绪”的组织占比则从 36% 降至 33%。大多数企业停留在部分就绪阶段：在数据部分就绪的企业中，57% 表示仅在局部获得投资回报，而在数据完全就绪的企业中，这一比例为 16%。数据就绪程度更高的组织，更有可能报告获得广泛、可重复实现的回报，而数据就绪程度较低的组织则落后。

第四季度调查的主要发现包括：

AI 持续进入生产应用阶段

  • 几乎所有企业（98%）都表示正在开展 AI 项目。
  • 增加支出的意愿遍及各地区：每个地区都有 60–68% 的企业预计将增加 AI 支出，其中美洲和西欧领先，两者均约为 68%。
  • 37% 的企业正将 AI 试点扩大到生产应用，高于第三季度的 34%。

数据就绪程度与 AI 投资回报密切相关

  • 数据已完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业，报告获得广泛或强劲 AI 投资回报的比例，是数据部分就绪企业的六倍以上（6.5 倍）。
  • 在企业数据已完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业中，81% 正获得广泛或强劲的投资回报；而在数据仅部分就绪的企业中，这一比例为 12%。
  • 仅看强劲投资回报，差距更大：数据完全就绪的企业中，55% 报告获得强劲投资回报，而在数据就绪程度低或完全未就绪的企业中，这一比例为 2%。
  • 从地区来看，东欧、亚太地区和西欧在广泛或强劲投资回报（30–31%），以及数据基本或完全具备 AI 应用条件的企业占比（41–43%）这两项指标上均领先，而美洲（分别为 23% 和 37%）和非洲（分别为 21% 和 33%）则落后。

AI 回报保持稳定

  • 28% 的企业报告获得广泛或强劲的 AI 投资回报，与第三季度持平。
  • 44% 的企业表示在部分 AI 试点中获得了“局部投资回报”，而仅有 9% 表示大多数试点已扩大应用规模并取得明确收益。

企业数据尚未完全准备好支持大规模 AI 应用

  • 8% 的企业表示，其企业数据已“完全就绪”，能够支持大规模 AI 应用。
  • 44% 的企业称其数据“部分就绪”，33% 称其数据“基本就绪”。

Kotovets 表示：“下一阶段的 AI 采用，将较少取决于能否获取模型，更多取决于这些模型可使用的信息质量。投资于经过验证的身份信息、相互关联的数据，以及可直接支持决策的背景信息的企业，将更有能力以更快的速度、更强的信心和更高的可控性扩大 AI 应用规模。”

邓白氏 AI Momentum 调查是一项每季度开展的全球调查，覆盖 32 个国家的 10,000 家企业，持续追踪企业 AI 采用、投资、部署及业务成果的变化。

关于邓白氏

邓白氏为企业大规模部署 AI 提供经过验证的商业身份基础。该公司于 1963 年创立 D‑U‑N‑S® 编码，如今该编码已成为识别商业实体的全球标准。以这一标识符为基础，D&B Commercial Graph™ 以一致的方式跨系统组织和关联企业身份信息，使 AI 能够基于准确、经过验证的数据运行。自 1841 年以来，各种规模的企业一直依靠邓白氏应对变化、加速增长。欲了解更多信息，请访问 www.dnb.com。

来源：Dun & Bradstreet, Inc.
